To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of the pro-apoptotic genes Bax and Fas, and the anti-apoptotic gene cIAP2 are upregulated in the liver of rats with CCl4-induced fibrosis.
cytokine stimulation of hepatocytes leads to a rapid increase in the anti-apoptotic protein cIAP2 and to a delayed increase in the pro-apoptotic protein Bax.
cytokines induce the expression of the NF-kappaB-dependent antiapoptotic gene cIAP2, which in turn inhibits cytokine-induced apoptosis in rat hepatocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of NF-kappaB in hepatocytes and its relationship with cytokine-induced apoptosis.
the regulation of pro- or anti-apoptotic proteins in hepatocytes and with the role of NF-kappaB in this regulation.
a better understanding of the mechanisms involved in the regulation of the cell death program in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no studies that support the notion that the presence or absence of a particular gene in a particular tissue is the cause of the development of the disease in question.
the effects of the cytokine on hepatocytes is dependent on the cytokine concentration, the duration of the cytokine exposure and the presence of the cytokine receptor.

the results obtained from this study indicate that the expression of the anti-apoptotic cIAP-2 gene in rat hepatocytes is regulated by the cytokine IL-6, and that cIAP-1, cIAP-3 and cIAP-4 are not expressed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified the first cytokines that induce anti-apoptotic proteins in rat hepatocytes and that these cytokines act through NF-kappaB to induce cIAP2 and that cIAP2 prevents apoptosis.
we are interested in the regulation of gene transcription by cytokines and transcription factors in hepatocytes.
we found that the NF-kappaB pathway is activated by TNFalpha, IL-6, and IL-1beta in primary hepatocytes and that NF-kappaB activation is required for TNFalpha-induced cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NF-κB signaling pathway regulates the expression of the anti-apoptotic protein cIAP2 in the rat liver and that the expression of cIAP2 is induced in hepatocytes by proinflammatory cytokines.
the anti-inflammatory cytokine interleukin-10 (IL-10) can prevent liver injury and death by preventing the release of tumor necrosis factor (TNF) and by inducing anti-apoptotic proteins.
we have shown that a combination of a small molecule and a small RNA can work together to inhibit a protein that is important for cell survival.
